narrativeReportMd:
# RiskAssessment R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`RiskAssessment` is still the same resource, but it has one hard local instance break: R4 `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` were removed and replaced by R6 `reason` using `CodeableReference`. Existing R4 JSON/XML that carries either old element name will not validate as R6 without transformation.

## Scope
The assessment covers local `RiskAssessment` elements and local terminology bindings. Inherited base-resource and datatype changes are out of scope and should be owned by their base artifact reports.

## Main migration themes
The main local migration theme is consolidation of parallel code/reference fields into `CodeableReference`. R6 also widens several domains: `status` can use additional Observation Status codes, `performer` can reference Patient or RelatedPerson, and `prediction.probability[x]` can now be a percent `Quantity`.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest R4-to-R6 validation break is the `reasonCode`/`reasonReference` merge. The highest R6-to-R4 risks are new required-binding status codes, `probabilityQuantity`, and `CodeableReference` content that cannot always be represented in the two R4 reason arrays without losing association.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for cross-version downgrade policies: mapping new Observation Status codes to R4, deciding whether `probabilityQuantity` can be converted to decimal or Range without losing comparator/unit semantics, and deciding how to handle an R6 `reason` repetition that carries both concept and reference.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Most R6 changes are widening changes for R4-to-R6 acceptance, but they create reverse-compatibility and runtime risks for generated code and R4 clients. The reason merge could have been less disruptive by retaining deprecated aliases, but it follows a broader FHIR modeling pattern toward `CodeableReference`.

## Follow-up analysis
Central cross-artifact mapping is recommended for Observation Status and CodeableReference, because the same patterns affect more artifacts than RiskAssessment.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `RiskAssessment` has one direct R4-to-R6 instance break: `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` are replaced by `reason`. The main migration concerns are reason transformation, new Observation Status codes, and R6-only `performer`/`probabilityQuantity` content. Confidence is high for structural changes and medium for exact downgrade policies because official ConceptMaps and narrative change notes were not supplied.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should treat `RiskAssessment.reason` as the required structural transform. R4 `reasonCode` values map naturally to `reason.concept`, and R4 `reasonReference` values map naturally to `reason.reference`. Downgrade from R6 to R4 needs policy for `CodeableReference` repetitions containing both concept and reference, new status codes, Patient/RelatedPerson performers, and percent Quantity probabilities.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for element presence, cardinality, type, reference target, and binding changes because both StructureDefinitions were present and directly compared. Confidence is lower for terminology semantics and best downgrade mappings because no official expansions, ConceptMaps, or ballot rationale were included.

findings.title: R4 reasonCode and reasonReference were replaced by R6 reason

oldState.summary: Two separate optional repeating elements represented reasons: `reasonCode` as CodeableConcept and `reasonReference` as Reference.

semanticText.definition: `reasonCode` was the reason the risk assessment was performed; `reasonReference` was resources supporting the reason the risk assessment was performed.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used the common parallel-field pattern: codes were carried in `reasonCode[]`, while references were carried in `reasonReference[]`.

newState.summary: A single optional repeating `reason` element represents either a concept or a reference by using CodeableReference.

semanticText.definition: The reason the risk assessment was performed.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses `reason[]` with `CodeableReference`, whose `concept` child is a CodeableConcept and whose `reference` child is a Reference.

facts.note: The referenced resource target set is preserved inside CodeableReference.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The two R4 elements have the same purpose text as the R6 `reason` element and the same reference target set. The R6 type directly combines a CodeableConcept concept and Reference reference, so this is a high-confidence merge.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct wire-format break for R4-to-R6 validation: `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` are no longer legal element names in R6. R6-to-R4 is also risky because `CodeableReference` can associate a concept and a reference in one repetition, while R4 has two independent arrays with no native way to preserve that pairing.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The reason for a risk assessment can affect audit, clinical explanation, and downstream decision support. Losing or mis-associating a reason code/reference pair could change the interpretation of why the assessment was performed.

justification.inferredGoal: Replace parallel code/reference reason fields with the newer CodeableReference modeling pattern.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated reasonCode and reasonReference alongside new reason, but only as a transition/alias pattern with reconciliation rules.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal--moving the reason model to `CodeableReference`--is reasonable because it unifies coded and referenced reasons and can keep concept/reference pairing within a single repetition. However, the break is real: R4 element names disappear. A less-breaking base design was available, but its duplication and reconciliation costs are material, so the breaking design is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking design would keep `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` in base R6 as deprecated aliases while adding preferred `reason` entries using `CodeableReference`. That would preserve existing R4 wire instances and allow new R6 content. The drawback is that the same reason could appear in old fields, the new field, or both; validators and serializers would need precedence/pairing rules, searches would need to cover both representations, and deprecated same-resource representations can linger indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves most R4 instances but creates duplicate same-resource representations, validation ambiguity, and indefinite support burden.

evidence.quote: The reason the risk assessment was performed.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `reasonReference` as `0..* Reference` to Condition, Observation, DiagnosticReport, or DocumentReference.
evidence.quote: Resources supporting the reason the risk assessment was performed.

evidence.detail: R6 defines `reason` as `0..* CodeableReference` with the same reference targets.
evidence.quote: The reason the risk assessment was performed.

evidence.detail: CodeableReference has optional `concept` and optional `reference` children.

examples.examplesMd: The examples are minimal fragments focused on the changed fields. A complete migration should also preserve array order within each old field and provenance of any policy-driven pairing decisions.

findings.narrativeMd: `RiskAssessment.reasonCode` and `RiskAssessment.reasonReference` disappear from the R6 resource and are replaced by `RiskAssessment.reason`. This is the main hard break for existing R4 instances because strict R6 validators and generated parsers will reject the old element names. The semantic payload is still supported, but it must be moved into `CodeableReference.concept` or `CodeableReference.reference`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance containing `reasonCode` or `reasonReference` can be valid in R4 and invalid in R6 because those element names are not present in the R6 content model. R6 content can usually be downgraded by splitting `reason.concept` to `reasonCode` and `reason.reference` to `reasonReference`; however, if one `CodeableReference` repetition carries both children, R4 cannot preserve their association without an extension or profile-specific convention.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, transform each `reasonCode` repetition to `{ "concept": <CodeableConcept> }` and each `reasonReference` repetition to `{ "reference": <Reference> }` under `reason[]`. For R6-to-R4, split concept and reference children into the two R4 arrays and decide how to record any lost association, for example with an extension, Provenance, or manual review when both children appear in one `CodeableReference`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change was probably justified by a cleaner shared pattern, but it was not wire-compatible. Keeping deprecated R4 element names alongside `reason` would have allowed old instances to validate while giving implementers time to migrate, at the cost of duplicated representations and reconciliation rules.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is recommended for R6-to-R4 downgrade policy when a single `reason` repetition contains both a concept and a reference.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 instances that carry `reasonCode` or `reasonReference` have an old-valid/new-invalid wire-name break in R6, where the base element is `reason` with `CodeableReference`. A straightforward R4-to-R6 mapper can usually emit one `CodeableReference` per old code or reference, but R6 can also pair a concept and a reference in one repetition, which cannot be represented with the same association in R4's two independent arrays. That is real migration work and can affect clinical explanation or audit trails, but the R6 design uses the common CodeableReference pattern to model concept-or-instance reasons directly, and keeping both old fields plus the new field would create duplicate representations and precedence questions.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition defines `RiskAssessment.reasonCode` as 0..* CodeableConcept and `RiskAssessment.reasonReference` as 0..* Reference(Condition, Observation, DiagnosticReport, DocumentReference).
R6 StructureDefinition defines `RiskAssessment.reason` as 0..* CodeableReference with the same reference targets.
R6 CodeableReference has optional `concept` and `reference` children.

Quick public check found implementation relevance: HL7 US eLTSS v2.0.0 R4 profile lists `RiskAssessment.reasonReference` in its profile definitions, but this is not definitive broad production deployment evidence (https://hl7.org/fhir/us/eltss/StructureDefinition-RiskAssessment-eltss-definitions.html).
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 RiskAssessment is trial-use/FMM 1, so the hard break does not by itself create a strong stability objection. The path is clinically explanatory and appears in at least one official R4 IG profile, so FMM softens but does not erase the migration concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus R6-to-R4 loss: old R4 element names are not legal R6 base elements, and an R6 CodeableReference repetition with both concept and reference loses its pairing if flattened to separate R4 arrays.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained deprecated `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` while adding `reason`, which would preserve more old instances. That alternative has material tradeoffs: two ways to express the same reason, possible conflicts, unclear precedence, and continued codegen/API burden. A StructureMap or migration guide is useful mitigation but is not a less-breaking base model.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high-impact assessment: the forward hard break and reverse pairing loss are real, but the existing report gives too little weight to FMM 1 and to the duplicate-representation cost of the obvious compatibility alternative.

findings.title: RiskAssessment.status required binding uses expanded R6 Observation Status codes

oldState.summary: `status` was a mandatory code with required binding to Observation Status version 4.0.1.

binding.description: The status of the risk assessment; e.g. preliminary, final, amended, etc.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R4 ValueSet includes the full local Observation Status CodeSystem by compose. No explicit expansion was present in the package.

semanticText.definition: The status of the RiskAssessment, using the same statuses as an Observation.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed the Observation Status codes present in the R4 code system, including `registered`, `preliminary`, `final`, `amended`, `corrected`, `cancelled`, `entered-in-error`, and `unknown`.

newState.summary: `status` remains mandatory and required, but the bound Observation Status ValueSet is version 6.0.0-ballot4 and includes additional codes.

binding.description: The status of the risk assessment; e.g. preliminary, final, amended, etc.

changedCodes.oldMeaning: Observation is complete and no further actions are needed.
changedCodes.newMeaning: Definition additionally mentions situations where there is a not-asked dataAbsentReason.

changedCodes.oldMeaning: Observation unavailable because measurement was not started or completed.
changedCodes.newMeaning: Adds expectation that a data absent reason should provide clarity.
changedCodes.changeSummary: Definition text adds conformance guidance from Observation context.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local CodeSystem concepts were compared directly. The ValueSet compose still includes the whole `http://hl7.org/fhir/observation-status` system, but no official expansion or cross-version ConceptMap was available.

semanticText.short: registered | specimen-in-process | preliminary | final | amended | corrected | appended | cancelled | entered-in-error | unknown | cannot-be-obtained
semanticText.definition: The status of the RiskAssessment, using the same statuses as an Observation.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the required binding but adds `specimen-in-process`, `appended`, and `cannot-be-obtained` to the underlying Observation Status code system used by the ValueSet.

facts.note: No R4 Observation Status code used by the ValueSet was found to be removed in the local R6 CodeSystem.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not an old-valid/new-invalid break because the R6 required binding appears to include all R4 codes. It is a high R6-to-R4 and runtime risk because `status` is mandatory and generated R4 enum parsers or validators will reject newly valid R6 codes.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Status drives lifecycle interpretation. Collapsing `appended`, `specimen-in-process`, or `cannot-be-obtained` to an R4 code can lose clinically relevant workflow meaning.

justification.inferredGoal: Align RiskAssessment with the newer Observation Status lifecycle vocabulary.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No R4-to-R6 backward-compatible alternative is needed because the status binding is widened and the R4 codes are preserved.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal--aligning `RiskAssessment.status` with the expanded Observation Status lifecycle vocabulary--is reasonable. The local terminology comparison found added R6 codes but no removed R4 codes, so this does not make old R4 instances invalid in R6. The remaining risk is that R6 instances using new codes need explicit downgrade policy for R4 systems.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because this is additive terminology widening, `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is not applicable under the calibration rules. Keeping the R4 code set and representing finer states with extensions could reduce R6-to-R4 enum failures, but that would be a reverse-compatibility mitigation and would weaken consistent base-level status semantics in R6, not a less-breaking way to preserve R4-valid instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 mapping and enum-parser risks remain, but they are downgrade/runtime costs rather than a less-breaking R6 base-design alternative for old R4 content.

evidence.detail: R4 binds `status` to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/observation-status|4.0.1` with required strength.
R6 binds `status` to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/observation-status|6.0.0-ballot4` with required strength.
R6 Observation Status contains additional concepts not present in R4: `specimen-in-process`, `appended`, and `cannot-be-obtained`.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example shows one possible lossy downgrade policy: map `appended` to the broader R4 `amended` status and preserve the original code in an extension. It is illustrative, not an official ConceptMap.

findings.narrativeMd: `RiskAssessment.status` still has cardinality `1..1` and a required Observation Status binding, but the underlying R6 code system is wider. This can surprise implementers because a required binding often appears stable at the element level while the set of legal code literals changes underneath.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances using old Observation Status codes should remain valid in R6 based on the local CodeSystem comparison. R6 instances using `specimen-in-process`, `appended`, or `cannot-be-obtained` will not validate against R4 without translation. Strict enum-based deserializers generated from R4 can fail at parse time before business logic sees the resource.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: R4-to-R6 migration does not need to change existing status codes. R6-to-R4 downgrade should use a deliberate mapping policy, likely mapping `appended` to `amended`, considering whether `specimen-in-process` maps to `registered` or `preliminary`, and deciding whether `cannot-be-obtained` maps to `cancelled`, `unknown`, or an extension-preserved value. Test all new R6 status codes against validators and enum parsers.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Adding codes to a required binding is backward compatible for R4-to-R6 validation but not for reverse compatibility or generated code. The less disruptive alternative would be extension-based finer states, but that would weaken uniform support for the new lifecycle distinctions in R6.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: No official ConceptMap was available, so downgrade mappings for new Observation Status codes require governance review.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The required binding remains ObservationStatus, and the R6 value set includes the R4 codes while adding more specific statuses such as `specimen-in-process`, `appended`, and `cannot-be-obtained`. Existing R4 instances remain valid with respect to this path when moving to R6. The concern is mainly that an R4 validator, generated enum, or down-converter will not accept a newly valid R6 status, but that is an additive terminology expansion rather than a forward compatibility break.
keyEvidence: R4 `RiskAssessment.status` is 1..1 code with required binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/observation-status|4.0.1`.
R6 `RiskAssessment.status` is 1..1 code with required binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/observation-status|6.0.0-ballot4`.

R4 ObservationStatus includes registered, preliminary, final, amended/corrected, cancelled, entered-in-error, and unknown; R6 retains those and adds statuses including specimen-in-process, appended, and cannot-be-obtained.
HL7 US eLTSS v2.0.0 R4 profile documents RiskAssessment status as mandatory and using the R4 ObservationStatus values (https://hl7.org/fhir/us/eltss/StructureDefinition-RiskAssessment-eltss.html).
freshReview.fmmEffect: Because the R4 resource is trial-use/FMM 1, the review should not escalate an additive code-system widening into a standards concern without evidence of common production breakage. The eLTSS check shows implementation relevance for `status`, but not enough to make the reverse-only issue high concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss/runtime/API/codegen only: R4 enums or validators may reject newly valid R6 codes, but old R4 status codes are still accepted by the R6 binding.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-expansive R6 design could have kept RiskAssessment on the R4 ObservationStatus subset, but that would diverge from the resource definition's stated alignment with Observation status and would prevent representing newer lifecycle states. Since the change is widening rather than narrowing, a less-breaking base alternative is not needed.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing high overall impact: the report correctly notes no old-valid/new-invalid break, but overstates the practical severity of an additive, reverse-direction terminology expansion for FMM 1 content.

findings.title: RiskAssessment.performer can now reference Patient or RelatedPerson

oldState.summary: `performer` was `0..1 Reference` limited to Practitioner, PractitionerRole, or Device.

semanticText.definition: The provider or software application that performed the assessment.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented performers as clinical professionals, roles, or devices/software.

newState.summary: `performer` remains `0..1 Reference` but additionally allows Patient and RelatedPerson.

semanticText.definition: The provider, patient, related person, or software application that performed the assessment.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 explicitly permits self-assessment or related-person assessment.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a widening change for R4-to-R6, so old instances are not invalidated. R6 instances that use Patient or RelatedPerson performers cannot validate as R4 without dropping, re-homing, or extension-preserving the performer. Generated code and business rules that switch on the R4 target set may also reject or ignore the new target types.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Performer identity is relevant for attribution and audit. The clinical risk is usually lower than changing the prediction itself, but losing a patient or caregiver performer can affect trust and accountability.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow self-assessment or caregiver/related-person assessment as first-class performer attributions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No R4-to-R6 backward-compatible alternative is needed because performer target profiles were widened while all R4 targets remain valid.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal--making patient self-assessment and related-person/caregiver assessment first-class performer attributions--is reasonable and is reflected directly in the R6 definition and target profiles. Since Practitioner, PractitionerRole, and Device remain allowed, the change does not invalidate R4 instances. The level of R4-to-R6 breakage is therefore effectively none.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: This target widening falls under the calibration rule for changes that preserve R4 instances, so a backward-compatible alternative assessment is not applicable. R6-to-R4 conversion can still choose to reject, drop, extension-preserve, or move Patient/RelatedPerson performers to Provenance, but those are downgrade policies rather than evidence that base R6 should have avoided the widening.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Patient and RelatedPerson performers create R6-to-R4 target-profile gaps, but extension or Provenance handling is downgrade mitigation rather than a base-design alternative for preserving R4 instances.

evidence.detail: R4 target profiles are Practitioner, PractitionerRole, and Device.
R6 target profiles add Patient and RelatedPerson.

examples.examplesMd: The example is valid against the widened R6 target set but not against the R4 performer target profile list.

findings.narrativeMd: `performer` is widened, not narrowed. R4 producers can keep sending Practitioner, PractitionerRole, or Device references, but R6 producers can now identify the patient or a related person as the performer.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4-valid instance becomes invalid in R6 because existing target profiles are preserved. An R6 instance with `performer.reference` pointing to Patient or RelatedPerson is not R4-representable in the base element and may fail R4 validation or generated target-union deserialization.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: R4-to-R6 requires no transform. For R6-to-R4, decide whether to drop unsupported performers, preserve them in an extension, represent attribution through Provenance, or reject downgrade when performer attribution is mandatory.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is mostly additive and likely justified. A backward-compatible alternative for R4 clients would have used extensions or Provenance, but that would make patient/caregiver performance less discoverable and less consistently validated in base R6.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 widens `RiskAssessment.performer` by allowing Patient and RelatedPerson in addition to the R4 Practitioner, PractitionerRole, and Device targets. This does not invalidate any R4 performer reference. R4-only consumers of R6 data may need to handle or reject the new target types, but the path is optional, attribution-oriented, and the change is a normal target-list expansion.
keyEvidence: R4 `RiskAssessment.performer` is 0..1 Reference to Practitioner, PractitionerRole, or Device.
R6 `RiskAssessment.performer` is 0..1 Reference to Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, RelatedPerson, or Device.

HL7 US eLTSS v2.0.0 R4 profile constrains performer to practitioner/practitioner role/device-related targets, showing implementation relevance but not evidence that new R6 targets would disrupt existing R4 exchange (https://hl7.org/fhir/us/eltss/StructureDefinition-RiskAssessment-eltss-definitions.html).
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 trial-use/FMM 1 further lowers stability pressure. With no forward invalidation and only optional reverse handling for new target types, FMM supports treating this as acceptable model evolution.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss/runtime/API/codegen only: R6 instances using Patient or RelatedPerson as performer do not fit the R4 target set, but R4-valid performers remain valid in R6.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: The R6 design is already the less-breaking form because it widens the target list instead of replacing or narrowing it. Keeping the old target set would avoid reverse-version surprises but would also block patient or caregiver self-assessment attribution.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing medium impact: the evidence supports a reverse-only widening concern with low practical risk, not a meaningful compatibility problem.

findings.title: prediction.probability[x] adds Quantity and a percent Quantity invariant

constraints.human: low and high must be percentages, if present

constraints.expression: probability is decimal implies (probability as decimal) <= 100

semanticText.definition: Indicates how likely the outcome is (in the specified timeframe).

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented numeric probability as either a bare decimal percentage or a Range whose low/high quantities must be UCUM percent.

newState.summary: `probability[x]` allows decimal, Quantity, or Range, and R6 adds an invariant requiring Quantity probabilities to be UCUM percent and <= 100.

constraints.human: low and high must be percentages, if present
Probability as a decimal must be <= 100
constraints.expression: probability.empty() or ((probability is decimal) implies ((probability as decimal) <= 100))

constraints.human: Probability as a Quantity must be <= 100%
constraints.expression: probability.empty() or ((probability is Quantity) implies (((probability as Quantity).value <= 100) and ((probability as Quantity).code = '%') and ((probability as Quantity).system = %ucum)))

semanticText.definition: Indicates how likely the outcome is (in the specified timeframe). Range SHOULD be expressed as a Quantity (with a unit of '%'), rather than as a decimal value to make sure the percentage semantics are clear.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds a `probabilityQuantity` JSON/XML choice and adds validation ensuring that Quantity probabilities use UCUM percent and do not exceed 100.

facts.newValue: ras-3: Probability as a Quantity must be <= 100%

facts.oldValue: Indicates how likely the outcome is (in the specified timeframe).
facts.newValue: Indicates how likely the outcome is (in the specified timeframe). Range SHOULD be expressed as a Quantity (with a unit of '%'), rather than as a decimal value to make sure the percentage semantics are clear.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The added type does not invalidate R4 decimal or Range instances. It does create a new R6 wire shape, `probabilityQuantity`, that R4 schemas and generated choice-type classes do not know. Some Quantity values can be converted to R4 decimal, but comparator, unit display, and extension details may be lost.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Probability is central to the resource. A lossy conversion of a threshold such as `<5%` to a bare decimal can materially change clinical interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent probability as an explicit percent Quantity to make unit semantics clear.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No R4-to-R6 backward-compatible alternative is needed because Quantity is an added choice type and R4 decimal/Range probabilities remain valid.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal--representing probability as an explicit UCUM percent `Quantity`--is reasonable because a bare decimal has implicit unit semantics and cannot carry comparator or unit metadata. R6 keeps the R4 decimal and Range choices and constrains only the new Quantity form, so the R4-to-R6 base-design breakage is not present even though R6-to-R4 conversion can be lossy.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Under the calibration rules, this type widening is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue. Continuing to use only decimal/Range plus an extension or profile for unit-bearing probabilities would avoid a new R6 choice branch for R4 clients, but that is a reverse-compatibility or implementation-burden mitigation, not a necessary less-breaking alternative for old R4 instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The new choice branch burdens R6-to-R4 conversion and generated choice unions, but those costs concern new R6 content rather than preservation of R4-valid instances.

evidence.detail: R4 choice types are decimal and Range.
R6 choice types are decimal, Quantity, and Range.
R6 adds an error invariant requiring Quantity probabilities to be <= 100 and UCUM percent.
evidence.quote: Probability as a Quantity must be <= 100%

examples.examplesMd: A simple percent Quantity with only `value`, `system`, and `code` can often be downgraded to `probabilityDecimal`. The example uses a comparator to show a case where R4 decimal would lose meaning unless an extension or Range convention is used.

findings.narrativeMd: `prediction.probability[x]` gains the `Quantity` choice type. This is a forward-compatible widening for R4 data, but it is a concrete serialization and code-generation change because the R6 JSON property `probabilityQuantity` did not exist in R4.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 decimal and Range probabilities remain accepted by the R6 type list. Valid R6 `probabilityQuantity` content is not natively representable in R4. R4 parsers may reject the new choice property, and generated choice unions need a new Quantity branch. R6 validators also apply `ras-3`, which requires percent UCUM coding and value <= 100 for Quantity probabilities.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, no transform is required unless implementers choose to normalize decimals to Quantities. For R6-to-R4, convert only simple percent Quantities to decimal when doing so is lossless enough for the use case; preserve comparator, extensions, and unit metadata with an extension or manual review when needed. Add tests for decimal, Range, valid Quantity, invalid non-percent Quantity, and Quantity over 100.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change improves semantic clarity but introduces a new choice representation. The backward-compatible alternative would be to keep the R4 choice set and document a preferred extension or profile, but that would not give all base R6 implementations a common unit-bearing field.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 definition text says `Range SHOULD be expressed as a Quantity`, which appears likely to mean probability should be expressed as Quantity. The computable type list and `ras-3` invariant are clear despite this wording oddity.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the R4 `decimal` and `Range` choices and adds `Quantity`, constrained to UCUM percent and value <= 100. That means old R4 probability values remain valid, while R6 can now send a new `probabilityQuantity` wire shape that R4 schemas and generated choice-type APIs will not recognize. For plain percent quantities, an R4 mapper can usually convert to `probabilityDecimal`; edge cases such as Quantity comparator, display/unit metadata, or extensions may be lossy. Because probability is central to a risk prediction, this is real reverse-version migration work, but the additive type is a proportionate way to make percentage semantics explicit.
keyEvidence: R4 `RiskAssessment.prediction.probability[x]` allows decimal or Range; decimal is constrained to <= 100 and Range bounds must be UCUM percent.
R6 `RiskAssessment.prediction.probability[x]` allows decimal, Quantity, or Range.
R6 adds invariant `ras-3`: Quantity probabilities must have value <= 100, code `%`, and UCUM system.

HL7 US eLTSS v2.0.0 R4 profile and example use RiskAssessment predictions for identified risks, but the fetched example does not use probability values (https://hl7.org/fhir/us/eltss/RiskAssessment-risk1.html).
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 trial-use/FMM 1 softens the compatibility burden, especially because this is an additive choice type rather than an old-valid/new-invalid change. The path is central when used, so the reverse conversion issue is still worth noting, but not enough to demand redesign.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss/runtime/API/codegen: R4 parsers and generated models do not have `probabilityQuantity`, and down-conversion can lose Quantity-specific qualifiers even though plain percent values map well to R4 decimal.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have avoided the new choice type and relied on decimal or Range plus documentation, but that would not provide an explicit percent Quantity representation. Adding Quantity while retaining decimal and Range is a relatively compatibility-preserving base design; profile-only or extension-only approaches would reduce base interoperability for the new representation.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing assessment: the report correctly identifies the new R6 wire shape and possible R6-to-R4 loss, but its high impact is stronger than warranted for an additive type on an FMM 1 resource.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, abstract flag, derivation, and `DomainResource` base are unchanged. Maturity/status changes are listed as non-breaking notable changes.
No retained local element changed min or max cardinality. The reason merge changes element identity but preserves the old repeating optional capacity as `reason 0..*`.

Type changes for `reason` and `prediction.probability[x]` are findings. Other retained local choice/type domains, including `occurrence[x]`, `prediction.when[x]`, `method`, `code`, `outcome`, `relativeRisk`, `mitigation`, and `note`, showed no material type narrowing.

The `performer` target widening is a finding. The target sets for `subject`, `encounter`, `condition`, `basedOn`, `parent`, `basis`, and the reason reference targets were otherwise not materially narrowed.

The new Quantity probability invariant is covered in the probability finding. The existing decimal `<= 100` and Range percent constraints remain materially equivalent for R4-representable content. Inherited `ele-*`, `ext-*`, and `dom-*` changes are out of scope.
No local `RiskAssessment` domain element changed `isModifier`. Inherited modifier-extension behavior is out of scope.
No retained local domain element showed a material `isSummary` change. The old reason elements and new `reason` are all non-summary.
No local fixed value, pattern value, or default value was found on RiskAssessment-specific elements in either version.
No local RiskAssessment-specific slicing change was found.
No primitive maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue change was found. Probability percentage limits are expressed as invariants and are covered under constraints and the probability finding.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Artifact metadata changed from draft/trial-use to active/normative
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This does not change instance shape or validation of RiskAssessment elements by itself.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance, conformance, and implementation-guide authors may treat the resource differently because R6 marks standards status as normative and status as active, while R4 had draft/trial-use metadata.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Example bindings now point to explicit Risk Assessment example ValueSets
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The binding strength is `example`, so conformant instances are not required to use these codes and old coded values are not invalidated by base validation.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Generated documentation, UI pick lists, test fixtures, and terminology-aware authoring tools may start showing R6 example sets for `method`, `code`, and `prediction.outcome`.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Risk Probability ValueSet metadata changed but the binding remains example strength
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `qualitativeRisk` remains `0..1 CodeableConcept` with an example binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/risk-probability`; example bindings do not constrain instance validity.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Terminology tooling may notice that the ValueSet metadata moved from draft-style R4 metadata to active/informative R6 metadata, but no local base validation break was found.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `RiskAssessment.reason` now depends on CodeableReference. Datatype-level conversion, validation, and serialization risks should be assessed in the CodeableReference report.
`RiskAssessment.status` uses Observation Status with required strength. A centralized R4/R6 terminology mapping is needed because the code system is shared by Observation-like artifacts.

The RiskAssessment snapshots include inherited DomainResource constraint expression/text changes. They are intentionally excluded here and should be owned by the DomainResource/base-artifact analysis.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff, ballot issue rationale, or change note was available locally for RiskAssessment. The report infers rationale from StructureDefinition deltas.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the official RiskAssessment R4/R5/R6 diff pages, ballot reconciliation notes, or Jira issues.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology findings rely on local ValueSet compose rules and local CodeSystem concepts. No terminology server expansion or official cross-version ConceptMap was used.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run official expansions for the R4 and R6 ValueSets and review HL7-maintained cross-version ConceptMaps.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 package is `6.0.0-ballot4` and marked not for publication in package metadata, so details may change before a final R6 release.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Re-run the assessment against the final published R6 package.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: SearchParameters, profiles, examples, operations, and CapabilityStatements were not assessed as findings, even though local package files show RiskAssessment search parameter changes such as `probability-quantity`.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Assign separate analyses for SearchParameters and implementation-guide profiles if migration scope includes query behavior.
